title: From Honor Flights to fallen heroes: How Alaska and Hawaiian honor those who have served
summary: Employees across Alaska and Hawaiian came together to help transport the remains of an unidentified World War II airman for possible identification, bringing one family closer to answers after generations of waiting. That same commitment to service continues year-round through Honor Flights, the Fallen Soldier Program and initiatives that help military talent build careers in aviation.
body_markdown:
The Military Veterans and Allies Business Resource Group plays a pivotal role in connecting current and future military and veteran employees across Alaska Airlines, Hawaiian Airlines and Horizon Air. Their employee-led efforts prioritize career development, education, awareness and networking opportunities throughout the year, while partnerships with transition assistance nonprofits like FourBlock, The Honor Foundation and COMMIT provide service members with valuable exposure and support as they prepare for the next chapter of their lives in the civilian workforce.


Alaska and Hawaiian also have a long history of recruiting military talent. In 2025, Alaska launched its[Military Technician Transition Program (MTTP)](https://news.alaskaair.com/company/alaska-airlines-expands-military-technician-transition-program-to-include-new-civilian-career-pathways-at-hawaiian-airlines/) and has since transitioned 13 active-duty service members and veterans into fulfilling aviation careers throughout the combined company. The MTTP program is critical in ensuring Alaska, the fourth-largest global carrier in the U.S., maintains the highest safety standards as it expands its network and fleet.


**To learn more about how Alaska Airlines supports active-duty military members and veterans, visit Alaska Airlines’**[salute to service page](https://www.alaskaair.com/content/about-us/social-responsibility/salute-to-service?srsltid=AYCX9vLjwBTNJ9J8NS_OojWa3y5uBktJem-p1TUeuK1wLRoupvOnLc59) **.**
